_meta.purpose: The context assembler's precedence rules, DECLARED as data rather than expressed in code. Changing this file changes what context a finding is composed from, with no code deploy.
_meta.how_to_change_precedence: Reorder 'ranking'. The list is applied left to right as a lexicographic sort key, so the first entry dominates. Moving 'freshness' ahead of 'confidence' makes recency outrank strength; removing 'source_type' makes a conversation chunk compete with a structured record on confidence alone.
_meta.hard_vs_soft: A dimension in 'budget_partitions' is a HARD tier: everything in a better tier fills the budget before anything in a worse tier is considered, so a worse-tier item can never displace a better-tier item that fit. A dimension in 'ranking' is a SOFT preference applied within a tier. 'observed outranks inferred' is deliberately hard (R16-B2 AC3); source-type precedence is soft by default so a highly-relevant conversation is not shut out entirely by the existence of any structured record.
_meta.unknown_values: A value absent from a rank table sorts LAST among that dimension, never first. An item earns precedence by declaring what it is — the same fail-safe rule the module applies to provenance and to undated freshness.
_meta.note_on_versioning: Bump 'version' when a change would alter composition for unchanged inputs, so a stored selection_log can be read against the rules that produced it.

_budget_partitions: Hard tiers, best first. Each named dimension must have a rank table below.
_ranking: Soft ranking within a tier, most significant first. 'candidate_id' must stay last — it is the stable tiebreaker that makes the package byte-identical run to run.
_origin_ranks: R16-B1's provenance spine: observed data outranks inferred. Lower rank wins.
_source_type_ranks: Structured records outrank conversational content. 'structured' is the knowledge graph and structured source records (incidents, issues, cases); 'prose' is documents and pages; 'code' is repository content; 'conversation' is chat threads. These four names match the retrieval substrate's content types plus the graph.
_freshness: R18-B2 freshness weighting. 'halflife_days' is the decay constant: context loses half its freshness weight every N days. 'exclude_stale' drops candidates whose source artifact changed and whose chunks are not yet re-embedded — the strongest exclusion, applied before the confidence floor, because outdated evidence must never be served as current.
_confidence_floor: Context below this confidence is excluded even when budget remains, so weak context never displaces strong context. 0.0 admits everything and lets the floor be a deployment choice rather than a hidden default.
_caps: Hard output bounds. entities/relationships mirror app/graph_constants.py — the enterprise-safety constants — and must not be raised here without changing that single source of truth.

caps._total_items: 2.0-B3 T2: the per-finding context budget across ALL kinds — what actually bounds an LLM prompt, since the per-kind caps sum to 45 and a prompt should rarely carry that much. UNCALIBRATED and therefore null (disabled) by default: no measurement of real prompt sizes against narrative quality exists yet, and a hand-set number here would silently trim every finding on the strength of a guess. The per-kind caps remain in force meanwhile, so over-budget selection and its drop record are exercised in production regardless. Set an integer to enable; the budget report then names what it dropped.

_kind_precedence: 2.0-B3 T2: when the per-finding TOTAL budget binds, kinds are trimmed from the LAST entry backwards. Graph structure is listed first because a finding stripped of its entities loses the subject the evidence is about; evidence chunks are the most substitutable, so they yield first.
